current_state: Single example-vendor binding behind an abstraction flag (EXAMPLE_FAILOVER_ACTIVE=1). The backup provider is configured but cold; no shadow traffic and no automated health probe.
target_state: Active multi-provider split with deterministic traffic allocation and automatic health-probe failover; both providers receive shadow traffic continuously so the cutover path is exercised end-to-end every day.
concrete_steps: Provision the secondary example-vendor account in a separate billing org with its own API key and store the key in the canonical secrets manager under a dedicated kid.
Wire shadow-traffic mirroring at the abstraction layer so 5% of production calls are duplicated to the backup with results compared offline.
Implement the active health-probe loop in the kye-failover-controller worker with a 30-second cadence and a 3-strike trigger.
Add the §0.3 evidence chain emission (kye.purpose.request.v1 ... kye.compliance.attestation.v1) on every cutover decision.
Run the first quarterly failover drill end-to-end and pin the drill envelope to WORM.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-traffic comparison shows < 0.5% semantic drift over a 30-day window.
Automated cutover triggered by simulated primary outage completes in < 60 seconds with no human intervention.
Quarterly drill envelope landed in WORM with verdict=ok and replay-proof verifiable from public keys alone.
no-spof-coverage gate sees the registry row fallback_status='full' with the path_to_full runbook archived (not deleted).
decision_needed: Commercial: confirm the backup-provider contract terms before step 1 can execute. Procurement-bound, not engineering-bound.
